answer: A farm that wants 71 keys as a result pays 71 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the river seed, the nebula timing is verifiable from the vertex record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 36 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is trivial once and expensive in bulk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
